primitives.name: Pitcher-Catcher Synchronization
primitives.verbatim_quote: Their work with one another is of the most vital interest to the success of the nine, for in it lies the best part of the strength of the battery.
primitives.assumptions: Perfect signal transmission between pitcher and catcher, no noise, binary outcome (successful out or hit)
primitives.breakdown_regime: Complete synchronization failure leads to zero defensive efficiency

layer2.mapping: Bayesian updating of conditional probabilities given sequential observations
layer2.telemetry: Probability of successful pitch type given catcher's signal

primitives.name: Sore Hands Pitcher Detection
primitives.verbatim_quote: The pitcher should tell the captain; for it is the pitcher who will notice the unavoidable wince that is the proof of a catcher's sore hand.
primitives.assumptions: Wince is a perfect diagnostic indicator, no false positives/negatives
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure to detect soreness causes injury escalation

layer2.mapping: Conformal anomaly detection via sequential observation residuals
layer2.telemetry: Residual pitch velocity change indicating catcher discomfort

primitives.name: Catcher Throwing Practice
primitives.verbatim_quote: If the catcher be a good judge of batsmen, and the pitcher be of a disposition inclining him to depend upon some one else, it is best that
primitives.assumptions: Throwing practice improves accuracy and speed, linear relationship with repetitions
primitives.breakdown_regime: Zero practice leads to poor arm strength and miscommunication

layer2.mapping: State-transition model for catcher throwing proficiency
layer2.telemetry: Throw error rate as function of practice sessions
